items.issue: skills/use-qwen/scripts/eval_harness/trees.py: _land rebuilds keyed = {_fold(key): key for key in links} on every call and on every recursive hop. _ancestor_crossing calls it once per proper prefix of every member and _refuse_colliding_landings calls it per member, so validation is now O(members x depth x links) with a Unicode normalize per key each time, where the old code did one dict lookup per hop. A tar with thousands of members and many symlinks gets slow. Fix: build the folded lookup once per validation pass, or cache it per links dict, passing it down the recursion via a private helper that takes keyed so the public _land signature stays as the contract pins it.

items.issue: skills/use-qwen/scripts/eval_harness/trees.py: _refuse_colliding_landings resolves its landings under fold=True but still compares raw spellings in its landings and files sets, so the collision rule is not independently fold-correct. Pat raised it as a silent-overwrite defect with the example links {L: Pkg} plus members L/f and pkg/f. Coordinator reachability check: NOT currently reachable. _refuse_colliding_landings runs first and misses it, but _ancestor_crossing then refuses L/f outright (symlink_landings = {fold(L)} = {l}; landing prefix L crosses slot l, so crossed & symlink_landings is non-empty and it raises "L/f is beneath an archive symlink"). Any member beneath an archive symlink is refused, which is what makes two divergent landings unreachable; without a symlink, landings equal raw names and the whole-name _fold check in _refuse_duplicate_or_crossing_members already catches case and normalization merges. So this is a latent fragility, not a live escape: the collision rule is covered only incidentally by the ancestor rule, and would stop being covered if the ancestor rule were ever narrowed. The docstring claim that it judges collisions for the merging host is stronger than what the sets actually do.
